chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Tatum waiting for everyone else to play before he sat down
summary: Collins argues Tatum waited his turn not to cut anyone, because once he played no one else could.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Art kind of liked to I'd like to kind of wait until everybody was through and then cut everybody down. I've heard stories about that.
I heard one here in Los Angeles, where he and Peterson --
-- were playing, alternating all evening, and it was supposed to be an even contest so Art went in and played "Little Man" said (inaudible) You've Had a Busy Day.
Busy day, that's right. Actually, I think why Art did that was because he knew after he played no one would play. It wasn't that he was going to cut any

one, no. But he knew that once he played the piano players wouldn't play, and he wanted to hear them also. But what could they play after he finished? You know, he was very humble, you know, it wasn't that. He knew that he was the president, I'm sure, but then he also knew that after he finished what could they play. So he had to wait until everybody -- he had to let everybody play and then play.
